entries.title: Tom and Huck

violence.summary: A murder victim is stabbed three times with a knife shown from behind and another character has a knife thrown into their back; a child-adult fight draws blood, children are threatened with guns and knives, nearly drown, and an adult repeatedly threatens to kill a child, with references to whipping and lynching.

language.summary: Profanity includes "jackass," "goddamn," "damn," and "hell," plus name-calling like "idle wastrel," "river trash," and a body-shaming "fat boy" taunt; the Native American antagonist is repeatedly called "Injun Joe."

romance.summary: Children develop crushes and discuss love and engagement, with chaste kissing and hand-holding.

drinking.summary: Characters drink at bars, one is known for heavy drinking, and a boy repeatedly smokes a pipe while other characters smoke tobacco throughout.

handoffNotes: A murder witnessed by children, an adult repeatedly threatening to kill a child, and references to child abuse/lynching are intense for the family catalog and may need prose context.
The ethnic slur "Injun Joe" used for the antagonist should be flagged for sensitivity review even though it is folded into the language category.

entries.title: We're Back! A Dinosaur's Story

violence.summary: Lots of cartoon action and scary images/music surround an evil villain, including a frightening circus with fiery dragons, bats, and a demon parade, plus chasing, capture, caging, forced transformation into monkeys, and a climax where crows appear to devour the villain.

language.summary: A few mild insults appear, such as "moron."

romance.summary: CSM's category label is none, though it notes mild flirtation between two child characters.

drinking.summary: Gentle dinosaurs are drugged to revert to fearsome behavior, two children are given a substance that turns them into monkeys, and the villain smokes.

handoffNotes: CSM's Sex/Romance label is none but its detail text notes mild child flirtation, a minor label/detail conflict.
Villain-driven scares (demon parade, forced transformation, threat of being devoured) may be intense for the film's young target audience and could need prose context.

GRIEF/LOSS: the plot centers on Littlefoot's grandfather contracting a disease described as lethal to any dinosaur, with his illness and threat of death driving the entire journey (he recovers by the end). language.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful language concern.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drugs, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: GRIEF/LOSS: a central character (Ash) is turned to stone and appears dead for several minutes before being revived; CSM explicitly calls out 'some characters appear to die' and flags this as not suitable for young children who cannot distinguish real from pretend violence/death. Strong candidate for prose context.
CSM also flags 'a lot' of Products & Purchases (games, toys, trading cards, action figures tie-ins), outside this app's 4-flag model but worth noting for context.

entries.title: Baby's Day Out

violence.summary: Slapstick-style violence as kidnappers experience falls, punches, slaps, and head/groin strikes; an extended scene depicts a man's crotch catching fire. Characters react to pain but realistic injury consequences are absent.

language.summary: Name-calling limited to terms like "moron" and "idiot."

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drugs, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: The plot centers on an unsupervised baby wandering dangerous real-world environments (traffic, construction zones) after a kidnapping attempt; CSM flags this premise itself, plus the baby's dangerous independent behavior, as a parental concern even though the tone stays comedic throughout and the baby is never harmed.

entries.title: Blank Check

violence.summary: A criminal threatens someone with a gun and threatens a man's family, men threaten to throw a kid off a roof, a boy bites a thug, brothers punch each other, a man drives his car over a bike, and a kid locks a man in a rolling cage and pushes him into a pool.

language.summary: CSM's category label is none; only very mild words like "butt" and "punk" appear.

romance.summary: Parents joke about intimate relations in front of their son, an adult woman kisses the 11-year-old protagonist on the mouth, and a child suggests an adult couple will have sex after their first date.

drinking.summary: Alcohol appears at an adult party.

handoffNotes: The romance category includes an adult woman kissing the 11-year-old protagonist on the mouth as part of a romantic-attention subplot; this age-inappropriate dynamic is worth flagging distinctly to a human reviewer beyond the numeric level.

violence.summary: Perilous scenarios with tangible results including traps, chemical burns, pokes in the flesh with prongs, and chase scenes where tiny characters face hammers or risk drowning in milk; no deaths occur and the action stays frenzied but fun.

entries.title: Dunston Checks In

violence.summary: Slapstick and rough-and-tumble pummeling including ear-biting, silly karate, and kitchen pots to the head; a kitchen knife is wielded and a large tranquilizer rifle is shot at the orangutan Dunston.

language.summary: A few mild swears, the worst of which are "hell" and "holy s--t."

romance.summary: CSM's category label is none, though it notes mild suggestiveness involving a massage scene and a teen boy's romantic interests, plus silly sexual humor involving older women aimed over young viewers' heads.

drinking.summary: A woman drinks from a hip flask, and the orangutan Dunston is given a cigar to smoke.

handoffNotes: The 'some' language level includes a partially-censored strong profanity ("holy s--t") that is more intense than typical for the app's family catalog and may warrant a closer look despite CSM's own 6+ age rating.
CSM notes sensitive children might worry about the orangutan's safety during the tranquilizer dart scene, though the outcome is not distressing.

entries.title: First Kid

violence.summary: Lots of comedic pratfalls (characters fall into walls, trip on floors, roller skate into a giant birthday cake), the protagonist is bullied and engages in two fistfights, and a climactic scene involves characters pulling guns as the main character faces a near-abduction.

language.summary: "Sucks" appears twice, "hell" once, and the protagonist is called a "dork" by school bullies.

romance.summary: CSM's category label is none; only brief nonsexual partial nudity occurs when the protagonist moons the press corps as a prank.

drinking.summary: Secret Service officers are shown at a bar holding and drinking beers early in the film, and one character appears quite intoxicated.

handoffNotes: A subplot involves an online stalker threatening the protagonist, escalating to a climactic near-abduction scene with drawn guns; CSM notes this is treated more for plot advancement than substantive discussion, but the real-world danger (stalking, attempted abduction of a child) may warrant prose context or sensitivity review beyond the numeric violence level.
